description.narrative: The project is an advocacy program designed to address the poor attitude of the citizens toward voting due to the low rate of PVC registration and collection in Nigeria, this is to address, reducing VOTER APATHY. In the 2019 general elections, the number of registered voters in Anambra state was 2,447,996, collected PVCs were 2,071,714, and uncollected PVCs were 376,282. The low figures have prompted the JDPC Awka Diocese project team to initiate this ELECTORAL PARTICIPATION CAMPAIGN- EPC. So far, only about 45% of people in Anambra state have collected their PVCs. Some complained about the rate of insecurity in the state between October and December as the reason why they have not collected their PVCs. As the 2023 general elections draw nearer, JDPC Awka is determined to see the number of voters increase to about 75% at the end of this project in March 2023. The major objective of the project is to address VOTER APATHY. We have also discovered that despite the level of PVC collection, those who have their PVC have also refused to vote during elections. The project is aimed at educating and mobilizing the general public in 6 LGAs in Anambra state on two factors that are interrelated but aimed at a singular objective. 1 Collection of PVC 2 Voter's participation. Collection of PVC + Voters participation ---------- REDUCING VOTER APATHY. The project will incorporate both the community structure approach and media ( Radio) to implement the project. Persons with disabilities (PWDs) will participate in the radio program as speakers, providing a strong voice in the electoral process, including providing credible information to address voter apathy for the vulnerable group. The funds will be channeled through Caritas Nigeria. However, the implementation will be done by JDPC AWKA. Caritas will transfer all the funds to JDPC Awka. CAFOD will monitor and accompany JDPC throughout the project, the partnership relationship has been fully established.
